newsitem.title: GERMANY: Danzas sees improved 97 Germany results.
newsitem.headline: Danzas sees improved 97 Germany results.

text.p: Danzas expects to achieve better results in Germany in 1997 after two years of losses, the freight company's new managing director Germany, Kristian Schleede said.
Danzas was already benefiting from corporate streamlining, which included 300 job losses, and improved economic prospects in Germany, he told Reuters in an interview.
"The results in the first quarter were satisfactory and I believe we are on the right path. It looks good," he added.
"The market is picking up but the pressure on prices will remain. We must offer market-orientated prices and value-added services," he said.

Danzas Germany, part of the Swiss-based Danzas group, made an operating loss of 18 million Swiss francs on net turnover of 887 million Swiss francs last year compared to a 1995 operating loss of 16 Swiss million francs on turnover of 923 million Swiss francs, the company's annual report showed.
Schleede, appointed managing director in April said last year's results were hit by the weak German economy, strong competition and falling freight rates.
Under company-wide European re-structuring, Danzas gave up unviable business in Germany, outsourced some freight handling and linehaul operations and cut jobs by 300 to just over 3,000 staff.
"We started turning the corner in Germany in 1996, (but) the (financial) results were still not satisfactory. The results will really first be felt this and next year," Schleede said.
The Eurocargo overland division, which saw worse results last year as rates fell, should improve this year through better productivity, he added.
Danzas maintained its position in intercontinental transport of air and sea cargo last year and aims to expand in this market, he said.
In logistics, five terminals were closed last year leaving 20 warehouses operated for clients, including DuPont Co and BASF AG.
Schleede noted: "I believe we are through the worst and are now going forward.
"There is a clear trend that industrial firms are concentrating on their core business and are looking for companies able to can offer tailor-made logistics services," he explained.
